name: Baldwin County Heritage Museum
description: Following a community festival in 1979, a group of citizens who wanted to preserve the farming history of communities in Baldwin County founded BCHM. After opening to the public, we have continued to gain exciting items from local donations. Baldwin County Heritage Museum got non-profit status after locals donated the land. Then, we raised funds, collected items, gathered research, and opened our doors on October 31, 1987. The museum still operates as a 501 (c) (3) non-profit organization with our workforce of volunteers. If you're a history buff looking to find out what life was like for residents of the area years ago, Baldwin County Heritage Museum has a collection of awe-inspiring appliances, farm equipment, and more for you to explore. If you want a glimpse of Baldwin County, AL as it developed, then our heritage museum is the place to go. The mission of the Baldwin County Heritage Museum is to preserve the culture of the farm communities of early Baldwin County through the creation of a home for historically significant buildings, documents, and artifacts from community life. We have collected artifacts and stories from the early farming communities in the area, including tractors, wagons, appliances and clothing. When you walk through our museum, you'll feel like you're stepping back in time. When you have a small group or class of students learning about local farming history, you should schedule a private tour. Our volunteer tour guides can provide a detailed history, answer questions, and guide you through our historic buildings. After enjoying a day of education and history, you can enjoy our beautiful outside picnic space. We also have a collection of historic buildings around Baldwin County that make beautiful venues for weddings and other celebrations.
